items.title: pip_install also names scipy, a package Slicer bundles

findings.title: pip_install also names scipy, a package Slicer bundles
findings.explanation: The check only reaches this branch when nibabel or scipy fails to import, but the command asks pip to install both. scipy ships with Slicer; if a user's scipy import is broken (or a resolver decides to satisfy a dependency), pip can replace or upgrade Slicer's bundled scipy in the shared environment, affecting other extensions. Only nibabel is actually needed from PyPI.
findings.suggestion: Install only the missing package, e.g. pip_install("nibabel"), and tell the user to reinstall/repair Slicer if scipy itself is missing.

findings.title: Runtime package installation via pip
findings.explanation: The module installs Python packages (`nibabel` and `scipy`) at runtime via `slicer.util.pip_install()` when the user opens or runs the module, without pinning versions or declaring them in `build_dependencies` / `EXTENSION_DEPENDS`. While `nibabel` and `scipy` do not bundle Qt or VTK, runtime installation can cause environment instability or version conflicts across Slicer sessions. Slicer extensions should ideally declare Python package dependencies in their extension catalog entry or build configuration so they can be bundled/installed via the Extension Manager build infrastructure.
findings.suggestion: Declare dependencies properly or ensure robust handling, although prompt-based installation is common in Tier 1 scripted modules.

findings.title: Unpinned pip install of 'nibabel scipy' can alter Slicer's bundled scipy
findings.evidence:
import nibabel  # noqa: F401
 import scipy  # noqa: F401
 ... slicer.util.pip_install("nibabel scipy")
findings.explanation: The check only tests whether each import succeeds. If nibabel is missing but scipy is present, the user-confirmed install still runs 'pip install nibabel scipy' with no version constraints, which can upgrade or change the scipy that Slicer and other extensions share.
findings.suggestion: Install only the missing package, and avoid touching scipy if it is already importable. Consider a version constraint compatible with Slicer's bundled scipy.

items.title: Automated test only checks imports; validation is two cases

findings.title: Automated test only checks imports; validation is two cases
findings.evidence:
"""Automated test skeleton. Since a real test requires actual VolBrain
    sample data (patient data, not shared in this repo), this only verifies
    that the module's dependencies import cleanly. Real validation lives in
    the CLI repo's docs/validation/ (two cases)."""
findings.explanation: The registered test cannot detect regressions in the segmentation logic, and README.md:81-97 reports Dice 0.56-0.66 on two cases with limits tuned on the scored cases. Users get a research-grade heuristic; the README and the module note do warn about this and ask for visual checking, so this is a maturity limitation rather than a defect.
findings.suggestion: Add a synthetic phantom test (a small label volume with a brainstem, 4th ventricle and CSF shell) that asserts non-empty masks and plausible volumes, so the CI test exercises the core code path.

items.title: Catalog entry tracks the mutable 'main' branch rather than a fixed commit

findings.title: Catalog entry tracks the mutable 'main' branch rather than a fixed commit
findings.explanation: scm_revision 'main' means the index builds whatever commit is on main at build time, not the commit that was reviewed (the review target is 39602329...). Branch references are permitted, but the reviewed source may not be what users receive later. I could not verify that the commit exists.
findings.suggestion: Pin scm_revision to the reviewed commit hash, or record that the reviewed revision is 39602329.

items.title: Existing scene node named "Cisterna volumes" is emptied

findings.title: Existing scene node named "Cisterna volumes" is emptied
findings.explanation: Any segmentation node in the scene that happens to carry this name - including one the user created or edited themselves - has all of its segments deleted on Calculate. The loss is in-scene only (no file is overwritten), but unsaved manual work can be destroyed without warning.
findings.suggestion: Track the node created by this module (e.g. keep a reference or use a dedicated attribute/name prefix) and only clear that node, or ask before replacing a node the module did not create.

findings.title: Existing 'Cisterna volumes' segmentation is silently wiped on every run
findings.explanation: _createSegmentation looks up any node named 'Cisterna volumes' and calls RemoveAllSegments on it. A user who has edited that segmentation, or who has a different node with that name, loses the content without a warning. This is data overwriting inside the user's scene, though not on disk.
findings.suggestion: Create a uniquely named node each run, or warn before clearing an existing node that the user may have modified.

items.title: Fallback pontomesencephalic junction can raise KeyError

findings.title: Fallback pontomesencephalic junction can raise KeyError
findings.explanation: pmj comes either from max(pons) (a key of ant) or from the fallback `top - round(18 / v1)` at line 315, which need not be a slice containing brainstem and therefore need not be a key of the `ant` dict built at line 312. On such data the analysis aborts with KeyError instead of a meaningful message; the widget catches it and shows the raw exception text.
findings.suggestion: Clamp pmj to the nearest slice present in `ant` (or use the nearest key) before indexing, and raise a descriptive ValueError if no brainstem slice qualifies.

items.title: Long computation runs on the GUI thread without progress reporting

findings.title: Long computation runs on the GUI thread without progress reporting
findings.explanation: run()/runSynthSeg() call the core analysis synchronously; the core performs per-slice distance transforms and repeated np.argwhere over the full volume (cisterna_core.py:325-336, 362-364, 384-386), which on a 1 mm T1 can take many seconds to minutes. During that time Slicer's UI is frozen with no progress bar and no way to cancel, which looks like a hang to the user.
findings.suggestion: Run the analysis in a CLI node or a worker thread with slicer.util.ProgressDialog / a progress callback, or at minimum show a busy cursor and document the expected runtime.

findings.title: Heavy computation runs on the GUI thread with no progress feedback
findings.evidence:
volumes = self.logic.runSynthSeg(t1Node, synNode)
 ... volumes = self.logic.run(t1Node, tissuesNode, structuresNode)
findings.explanation: run_cistern_analysis and run_cistern_analysis_synthseg (per-slice distance transforms over full volumes) execute directly in the Qt click handler. The UI freezes for the duration, and only one processEvents call precedes the work. Large 0.7 mm volumes make this noticeable.
findings.suggestion: Show a busy/progress indicator, or run the numeric core in a worker thread. At minimum, document the expected run time.

items.title: README testing section describes v1 results; the shipped v2 code has no recorded Slicer validation

findings.title: README testing section describes v1 results; the shipped v2 code has no recorded Slicer validation
findings.evidence:
Both runs confirm the Slicer extension and the CLI tool (`cisterna_core.py`)
stayed in sync. These numbers were produced with method v1; the CLI repo has not
been updated to v2 yet.
findings.explanation: The README states that live testing in Slicer 5.11.0 matched the CLI, then says 'These numbers were produced with method v1; the CLI repo has not been updated to v2 yet.' The vendored cisterna_core.py is v2 (its docstring says 'method v2'). Users may assume the v2 code has been tested in Slicer when it has not.
findings.suggestion: Re-run the Slicer live test on the v2 code and update the README, or state clearly that the Slicer path is untested for v2.

items.title: Segmentation input with no segments yields an unhelpful TypeError

findings.title: Segmentation input with no segments yields an unhelpful TypeError
findings.explanation: If the selected vtkMRMLSegmentationNode contains no segments, arr stays None and is returned; runSynthSeg then calls np.unique(seg) on None, producing a TypeError instead of the intended "no 'csf' or 'brain-stem' segment" message. The user sees a confusing error in the dialog.
findings.suggestion: Raise the descriptive ValueError when arr is None (or when the segment count is zero) before returning.

items.title: Temporary resampled volume leaks if the analysis raises

findings.title: Temporary resampled volume leaks if the analysis raises
findings.explanation: The resampled T1 node is removed only on the success path; if run_cistern_analysis_synthseg raises (e.g. missing brainstem/4th-ventricle landmark), the temporary volume stays in the scene and is saved with the user's MRB, silently adding a duplicate volume.
findings.suggestion: Wrap the analysis in try/finally and remove the temporary node in the finally block.

items.title: Test is a bare import check with no functional coverage

findings.title: Test is a bare import check with no functional coverage
findings.explanation: The only automated test checks that cisterna_core has a run_cistern_analysis attribute. No synthetic volume exercises the mask logic, axis handling, or volume arithmetic, so regressions in the vendored core would go unnoticed.
findings.suggestion: Add a small synthetic-phantom test that checks voxel counts and orientation handling, using generated data rather than patient data.

items.title: Vendored copy of cisterna_core.py must be kept in sync manually with an external repo

findings.title: Vendored copy of cisterna_core.py must be kept in sync manually with an external repo
findings.evidence:
copy of this file is vendored inside
the Slicer extension ... if you change the logic, update BOTH copies.
findings.explanation: The docstrings say the source of truth is src/cisterna_core.py in a separate CLI repo, and that both copies must be updated by hand. Nothing in this repo checks this, so the Slicer and CLI results can silently diverge, as the README already notes for v1/v2.
findings.suggestion: Add a checksum or sync test, or move the shared core into one place both projects depend on.

items.title: Module directory inserted at the front of sys.path

findings.title: Module directory inserted at the front of sys.path
findings.explanation: Inserting at position 0 makes the extension directory shadow every other path entry for the rest of the Slicer session. The directory only contains CisternaMagnaVolumetry.py and CisternaMagnaVolumetryLib, so the practical risk is low, but appending instead of prepending would be safer.
findings.suggestion: Use sys.path.append(moduleDir) or rely on the path Slicer already adds for scripted modules.

items.title: Possible leaked temporary MRML node and silent NaN in CSF refinement

findings.title: Possible leaked temporary MRML node and silent NaN in CSF refinement
findings.explanation: In runSynthSeg, the resampled T1 node is removed only on the success path, so an exception from run_cistern_analysis_synthseg leaves it in the scene. Separately, refine_csf_with_t1 takes np.median over possibly empty arrays, which returns NaN and quietly disables the refinement without any warning. Both are minor robustness issues.
findings.suggestion: Guard the empty-selection case and log a warning. Remove the temporary node in a finally block.
